context: Request: past patent-infringement matters where the firm retained a technical expert, with the documents showing each retention (expert roster for a new patent case). Rubric: 1007-00003 (Vantage Mobility, Dr. Yeoh; proof: litigation-status-memo), 1014-00003 (Whitfield), 1014-00004 (Ashford) and 1037-00004 (Ostrowski), each with proof documents, plus a precision criterion (1013-00005 draft-only is tolerated).

stages.note: Reads 22 documents (status memos, retention agreements, engagement letters, complaints) across the shortlisted and sibling matters, one mistyped path, a folder listing to fix it, and two more read batches. The review flags a draft-only matter counted as qualifying.
Attempt 3: filtered listings of the ten remaining case-type matters; none added.

Re-reads the response, a path check fails on the workspace root, and fixes one spelling error.
Attempt 2: path check passes against the output folder; re-reads the openings of eight cited documents.
Attempt 3: re-reads the response end to end; no edit.
Calls finish.

first_error.critic_note: (generic flag) The scan review at [31] warned that the hand-picked shortlist risked dropping matters and named this matter, but only as a weak hit matched by a privilege-log memo.
first_error.why: The matter appeared in the path scan at [29] with a case-type analysis file and a retention memo, but the agent left it out of the eleven matters it listed and never opened it.

divergence: Mixed (T0 passes; T1, T2 fail on the same matter). All runs found the three matters with retention agreements. They split at the candidate-listing stage: T0 listed all files of the matter whose retention shows only in a status memo and read that memo; T1 listed it through a keyword filter that showed two files and read nothing; T2 never listed it. The reviews there did not differ in substance: none asked to open that matter (T2's review named it only as a weak hit), and later reviews told the agent to keep the matter set.
